correctness.rationale: For every real bounded c_0(Gamma)-to-c_0(Lambda) map, rows belong to ell_1 and fixed columns vanish at infinity. A monotone input increment has each coordinate in [0,1], giving the signed-row q bound. Finitely many scalar row pairings become Cauchy, so only escaping rows contribute to the asymptotic norm diameter. An induction selects escaping rows with large q and negligible previous finite input support, and finite maximizing-sign blocks. Their partial indicators form one increasing unit-ball sequence attaining every tail scale up to arbitrary epsilon. Finite output projections yield the independent exact essential-norm formula. The identity and signed block-difference operators attain the two comparison constants. Net-to-order implications are independently proved using compact uniform row envelopes. No finite numerical experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural quasi-Levi convergence test asks about increasing bounded vectors. Quantifying its maximal norm-Cauchy failure is mathematically motivated, and the theorem determines that invariant for the entire real c_0(Gamma)-to-c_0(Lambda) class, without separability or positivity. Its positive/negative row-mass formula yields a sharp and structurally meaningful factor-of-two interval versus essential norm, realized by explicit infinite operators. This is a new quantitative separation rather than a routine qualitative compactness corollary or a contrived finite computation.
